title: How Coca-Cola Really Makes Money (It Doesn't Bottle Most of It)
description:
People drink about 2.2 billion servings of Coca-Cola company drinks every day, yet the company doesn't bottle most of them. In this file we open the money machine behind Coca-Cola: a pharmacy in Atlanta in 1886 and only nine drinks a day, Asa Candler's $2,300 buy, the 1899 bottling deal that built the system, the contour bottle, the secret formula used as loan security and kept in a vault, the WWII five-cent promise, the New Coke mistake, the concentrate model and its high margins, why it sold off its own bottling plants, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: The Coca-Cola Company Q3 2026 results (October 2026); The Coca-Cola Company Q4 and full year 2025 results (February 2026); The Coca-Cola Company 2025 Form 10-K; The Coca-Cola Company, "The Coca-Cola System"; Coca-Cola company history pages (The Birth of a Refreshing Idea; The Asa Candler Era); Coca-Cola press release on the secret formula vault (December 2011); CNN Money (2011); New Georgia Encyclopedia (Coca-Cola Company).

All figures are rounded. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
